claims.title: Complete finite deterministic robust prefix-code universe
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph, finitely many exact rational source priors, and deterministic one-shot binary-prefix zero-error codes below declared search caps
assumptions: zero-error encoders are independent-set partitions of the confusion graph
every robust objective is coordinatewise nondecreasing in state codeword lengths
unary tree nodes may be contracted and a full binary tree with k leaves has maximum depth at most k minus one
nonclaims: the bounded exponential universe is not a scalable polynomial-time algorithm
prefix framing, one-shot operation, and declared-state zero error are explicit model assumptions

claims.title: Exact finite deterministic minimax length and minimax regret
claims.scope: the complete bounded deterministic code universe under a finite nonempty set of rational prior scenarios
assumptions: scenario expected lengths are computed exactly from state lengths and priors
equal cost vectors are deduplicated and only Pareto-dominated vectors are removed
scenario-specific oracle costs are exact minima over the same complete code universe
nonclaims: minimax absolute length and minimax regret are not assumed to select the same codebook
the finite scenario set is not a learned or universal prior model

claims.title: Convex-hull control by finite prior scenarios
claims.scope: source priors in the convex hull of a finite rational scenario set under fixed deterministic or shared-randomness code designs
assumptions: expected length is linear in the source prior
the prior-specific oracle value is a pointwise minimum of linear code costs and is therefore concave
nonclaims: the result does not cover uncertainty sets larger than the declared convex hull
online drift, dependence, and estimation error require separate source-process models

claims.title: Exact shared-randomness minimax game with sparse support
claims.scope: a finite rational matrix of prior-scenario costs for complete deterministic zero-error codebooks
assumptions: encoder and all decoders share a source-independent seed selecting the complete codebook
primal and dual support systems are exhaustively enumerated below the declared basis cap
every omitted primal and dual inequality is checked exactly
nonclaims: private encoder randomness is not treated as shared codebook knowledge
the certificate bounds codebook support by the number of scenarios but does not price exact non-dyadic random-seed generation

claims.title: Least-favorable barycenter identity for shared-randomness minimax length
claims.scope: the complete bounded deterministic code universe and the convex hull of finitely many rational source priors
assumptions: the dual scenario mixture forms a barycenter prior
expected code length is linear in the prior
the exact primal and dual finite-game values agree
nonclaims: the identity is for minimax expected length and is not transferred to peak length or nonlinear queueing loss
the regret dual retains the explicit mixture of scenario-oracle baselines

claims.title: Finite-prior robust coding hierarchy
claims.scope: deterministic and shared-randomness zero-error prefix codes for one finite confusion graph and finite prior scenario set
assumptions: scenario oracle values use the same complete deterministic code universe
a fixed-length minimum coloring is an admissible deterministic prefix code
shared-randomness mixtures include deterministic point masses
nonclaims: absolute minimax value and minimax regret value have different baselines and are not numerically ordered against each other
an expected-length bound is not hard one-shot network feasibility

claims.title: Three-state strict shared-codebook-randomness gain
claims.scope: the complete three-state confusion graph with priors (4/5,1/10,1/10) and (1/10,4/5,1/10)
assumptions: a shared seed may select between complete deterministic prefix codebooks before the source state is observed
every selected codebook remains zero error on all declared states
nonclaims: the zero-error message alphabet remains three
the strict gain is in worst-prior expected length and consumes shared codebook randomness

claims.title: Four-state robust minimax tree is not a scenario oracle
claims.scope: the complete four-state confusion graph with two priors concentrating probability seven tenths on different states
assumptions: all complete binary prefix trees are included
absolute deterministic minimax expected length is the objective
nonclaims: a balanced tree is not universally minimax under prior uncertainty
enumerating only scenario-specific Huffman trees is not generally complete

claims.title: Minimax expected length and minimax regret select different four-state codes
claims.scope: the declared complete four-state graph with priors (1,1,1,7)/10 and (1,2,5,2)/10
assumptions: all deterministic complete prefix trees are exhausted
regret subtracts each scenario's exact prior-specific oracle value
nonclaims: neither robust objective is declared universally preferable
the separation concerns expected prefix length rather than decoding accuracy

claims.title: Bounded exact finite-prior robust coding and game audit
claims.scope: bounded finite graphs, complete binary trees, rational prior scenarios, and finite rational zero-sum games checked by the repository
assumptions: all configured partition, shape, candidate, dominance, and game-basis searches complete
independent tests enumerate every coloring and complete tree on all sixty-four labeled four-vertex graphs
primal and dual game mixtures have exactly zero rational gap
nonclaims: bounded exhaustive agreement is not a large-instance runtime guarantee
a cap failure is not an optimum or impossibility certificate
